name: Level - Order Of Generic Tree
html:
Welcome Back Reader!

We hope that you are finding data structure, Generic trees easy to grasp. How did it go with Post and Pre traversal? Wasn't that interesting? In this article also we look at another way of traversing a Generic Tree. Yes, as the title says, Level Order Traversal.

If you have successfully understood the previous traversal then this one is going to be as easy as counting. You can first give this problem a try. Before you become restless for How and Why, let's get started with the problem.

Important Links : Problem Link, Question Video, Solution Video

Problem Discussion :

In this problem you are given a partially written GenericTree class.

All you need to do is to complete the body of the levelorder function. The function is expected to visit every node in "levelorder fashion" while printing the tree top to bottom levels from left to right where the nodes are separated by spaces.

Input is managed for you.

Consider the following example for better understanding of what needs to be done:

A generic tree is given to you with root 10 and its children as 20, 30 and 40. At level 1 there is only one element, 10. So first of all 10 is printed. At level 2, 20, 30 and 40 are present, so these get printed from left to right. Further, at level 3, we can spot only children of 30 which are 50 and 60. So, at last both of these get printed.

Please check the question video for better understanding.

Watch video Approach :
  • The problem here deals with printing the tree in levels from left to right where the nodes are separated by spaces.
  • We will use Queue to solve this problem. Yes! Queue.
  • Initially the root of the generic tree is added to the Queue. If we consider the above example then it means that 10 gets added to the queue.
  • After that we use a rule; RPA: Remove, Print and Add to operate the queue.
  • This rule says that, remove the element from the queue, print that element and then add its children to the queue.
  • So, talking of the example, 10 gets removed from the queue, get printed and after that its children 20, 30 and 40 are added to the queue.
  • After that we keep repeating the rule, RPA until the queue is emptied.
  • So the next element to get removed and printed is 20. Since there is no child of 20, we add nothing to the queue this time.
  • Next element is 30. It is removed and printed. Then its children 50 and 60 are added to the queue.
  • After that 40 is removed and printed. As there is no child of 40, nothing is added to the queue.
  • Next element is 50. It's removed and printed. 50 too have no child.
  • Next element is 60. It's removed and printed. 60 too have no child.

Let's try to code this.

  1. A Queue is defined as a type node.
  2. A node (basically root), passed as argument, is added to the queue.
  3. A while loop is applied which runs until the queue is emptied.
  4. An element (of type node) is removed from the queue and stored in the node.
  5. The node which was removed in the previous step, its data gets printed in this step.
  6. Then the children of this node are added to the queue using a for loop.

Yes, that looks perfect!!

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { private static class Node { int data; ArrayList< Node> children = new ArrayList< >(); } public static void display(Node node) { String str = node.data + " -> "; for (Node child : node.children) { str += child.data + ", "; } str += "."; System.out.println(str); for (Node child : node.children) { display(child); } } public static Node construct(int[] arr) { Node root = null; Stack< Node> st = new Stack< >(); for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { if (arr[i] == -1) { st.pop(); } else { Node t = new Node(); t.data = arr[i]; if (st.size() > 0) { st.peek().children.add(t); } else { root = t; } st.push(t); } } return root; } public static int size(Node node) { int s = 0; for (Node child : node.children) { s += size(child); } s += 1; return s; } public static int max(Node node) { int m = Integer.MIN_VALUE; for (Node child : node.children) { int cm = max(child); m = Math.max(m, cm); } m = Math.max(m, node.data); return m; } public static int height(Node node) { int h = -1; for (Node child : node.children) { int ch = height(child); h = Math.max(h, ch); } h += 1; return h; } public static void traversals(Node node){ System.out.println("Node Pre " + node.data); for(Node child: node.children){ System.out.println("Edge Pre " + node.data + "--" + child.data); traversals(child); System.out.println("Edge Post " + node.data + "--" + child.data); } System.out.println("Node Post " + node.data); } public static void levelOrder(Node node){ Queue< Node> queue = new ArrayDeque< >(); queue.add(node); while(queue.size() > 0){ node = queue.remove(); System.out.print(node.data + " "); for(Node child: node.children){ queue.add(child); } } System.out.println("."); } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); int[] arr = new int[n]; String[] values = br.readLine().split(" "); for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { arr[i] = Integer.parseInt(values[i]); } Node root = construct(arr); levelOrder(root); } }
java; true"; Analysis: Time Complexity:

O(n)

We travel to all the elements of the tree. Every node is processed individually in a while loop.

Space Complexity:

O(n)

A queue of size n will be used.
